findings.title: Deleting cache does not invalidate the displayed calendar cache status
findings.body: The delete-cache mutation only invokes the optional onSuccess callback. Unlike the disconnect mutation, it never invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. In this wrapper `onChanged` is optional, so after a successful deletion the active query can retain its previous `cacheUpdatedAt` indefinitely (window-focus refetch is disabled), continuing to show cache status and the delete action for data that no longer exists. Invalidate or refetch `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` when the deletion settles.

findings.title: The cron development command relies on an undeclared, unpinned tsx executable
findings.body: `tsx` is not declared in this workspace's dependencies or devDependencies, so `npx tsx` must resolve/download whatever current registry version is available when the command is run (and can fail in offline/CI or non-interactive environments). This makes `yarn dev:cron` non-reproducible and can execute an unexpected version. Add a pinned `tsx` dependency and invoke its workspace binary (or use the existing declared runner).

findings.title: The env-file update command fails on GNU/Linux sed
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E ...` uses BSD/macOS `sed` syntax. On GNU sed, which is used by typical Linux development and CI environments, the separated empty argument is treated as an input filename (or otherwise causes an error), so an existing `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` is not updated. Use a portable temporary-file replacement or select the `sed -i` form based on the platform.
